source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #381 (branch fix/193-register-mapping at head efa4f04b9ff6648a078edc7b5cf8464f7f253896 — the #193 change (the masm trait’s explicit per-target register mapping, phys_loc(vreg) -> PhysLoc { Reg | Slot }, homing the x86_64 and riscv64 virtual registers in physical registers instead of emulating the A64 register file in frame slots) merged with current main 9b7b4d4d3d168a25d4f82a3214cf1b32549f04d2 (PR #379 and PR #382), plus a size-gate re-baseline; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45806009119, 45806021489 and 45806033696 against the branch produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #381 (#193, per-target physical register mapping for the x86_64 and riscv64 baseline-JIT encoders). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45806043868, 45806057168 and 45806068026 on main at 9b7b4d4d3d168a25d4f82a3214cf1b32549f04d2 (PR #379 and PR #382); all three runs pass the gate; the main control is byte-identical to the checked-in baseline on the twelve series of the baseline, core and core-nosimd configurations, measures below it on the core-aot series (104 B / 16 B in release and 160 B / 64 B in release-size) and on the core-jit series (2,824 B / 1,600 B in release and 1,496 B / 512 B in release-size — the shrink from PR #382’s removal of the mmap-rs dependency from Unix builds of telomere-jit-codegen, independently measured by the #380 lane at −2,808 B on the release stripped file series), and measures below the retained baselines on the twelve series of the three configurations that link telomere-component). This PR’s own delta against the main control is confined to the core-jit configuration: in release, stripped file +12,864 B and stripped .text +9,408 B; in release-size, stripped file +5,704 B and stripped .text +3,536 B — the physical-register encodings and the in-place / register-destination forms in the x86_64 and riscv64 baseline encoders of telomere-jit-codegen, which only the core-jit configuration links with the jit feature. Every other series is byte-identical to main in both profiles. Against the checked-in baseline all four core-jit series grow (by 10,040 B / 7,808 B in release and 4,208 B / 3,024 B in release-size, the branch delta net of PR #382’s shrink already on main), so only those four series are re-baselined to the branch measurements and every other baseline is retained, following the established practice of re-baselining growth only. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples; the pull-request run 45806003564 at the same head measured byte-identically to the branch samples on every series. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release component stripped file series at +11.42% (2,433,656 B to 2,711,648 B), unchanged because that series’ baseline is retained; the re-baselined core-jit series stand at +8.32% (release stripped file, 1,989,584 B to 2,155,080 B), +7.48% (release stripped .text), +4.57% (release-size stripped file) and +4.23% (release-size stripped .text). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
